Subject: Recap + POC planning: next steps and success criteria

Hi Sara / Carlos —

Great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed POC plan so we all have alignment before we kick off:

1) Goals / success criteria (agreed):
- Integrate Redwood text-generation API for product description generation in the Acme CMS workflow.
- Latency requirement: median end-to-end generation <= 600ms for 512 tokens in US region.
- Quality: 90%+ pass rate on the checklist (relevance, no hallucinations on SKU fields) across 200 test prompts.
- Cost target: average per-1k-token cost below the threshold we discussed (internal metric).

2) Scope of POC (4 weeks):
- Week 0: access + onboarding (API keys, test account, required infra).
- Week 1-2: integration (SDK + streaming for progressive render) and initial tuning.
- Week 3: run evaluation suite (200 prompts) and quality/regression analysis.
- Week 4: wrap-up, SOW/next steps decision.

3) Owners:
- Acme: Sara (product lead) / Carlos (engineering) — own test prompts, data samples, success sign-off.
- Redwood: Marissa (sales lead) / Rishi (solutions eng) / Monica (CS lead) — own integration support, baseline configs, and evaluation scripts.

4) Deliverables:
- POC plan PDF (attached) with timelines and acceptance criteria.
- Integration checklist (attached).
- Temporary test keys and a sample dataset to be exchanged over secure link.

Next steps:
- Sara: confirm acceptance criteria and any additional constraints (PII redaction, KMS requirement) by EOD Thursday.
- Carlos: share engineering contacts + preferred dev environment (k8s, on-prem, etc.).
- Redwood: Rishi will send an integration playbook and prep a short demo of streaming responses + tool calling before dev work begins.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Redwood integration plan + API examples (for Acme)

Hi Carlos / Sara —

Per the ask, mapping out an integration plan and the implementation steps we recommend for the POC. High level first, then concrete examples below.

Integration plan (target: 2-week dev sprint):
- Day 0: Provide test org, generate ephemeral API keys, share SDK quickstart and playbook.
- Day 1-3: Implement server-side integration using Redwood SDK (Node or Python).
- Day 4-7: Add streaming endpoints to support progressive render in Acme CMS editor.
- Day 8-10: Enable tool-calling for SKU lookup & validation (we will provide a sample webhook adapter).
- Day 11-14: Run evaluation suite, tune prompts, and finalize acceptance report.

Success criteria (technical):
- End-to-end median latency <= 600ms for 512 tokens (US region).
- Streaming starts delivering first token within 150ms for most prompts.
- Tool calls for SKU validation complete within 200ms 95% of the time.

Sample SDK quickstart (Node):
- npm install @redwoodinference/sdk
- const Redwood = require('@redwoodinference/sdk');
- const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.RDW_TEST_KEY });
- // simple generate call
- const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-gen-1', prompt: 'Write product description for SKU: 12345' });

Recommended API routes (server-side):
- POST /api/generate -> proxy to Redwood generate endpoint. Returns full JSON when complete.
- GET /api/stream?prompt=... -> opens SSE / websocket to stream partial tokens to the editor UI.
- POST /api/tool/sku-validate -> receives tool call from the model, calls internal SKU service, returns structured validation JSON.

Streaming example (SSE):
- Client connects to /api/stream with Authorization header. Server forwards to Redwood streaming endpoint and relays chunks as they arrive. Include reconnection logic.

Tool calling flow:
1) Model issues a tool call in JSON schema form (e.g., {"name":"sku_lookup","args":{"sku":"12345"}}).
2) Redwood routes the tool call to /api/tool/sku-validate on your side (authenticated).
3) Your service replies with structured data (availability, title, attributes).
4) Model uses the tool response to continue generation.

Security & KMS notes:
- We support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration for Dedicated / Private deployments; for hosted POC we'll provide encrypted-at-rest defaults and can enable KMS-backed keys if required.
- Ephemeral test keys can be rotated via the console API (short TTL).

Attachments: I attached a short playbook (acme-poc-plan-v1.pdf) and a requirements checklist. I can also put a small sample Node + Python repo in the shared Drive if you want.

If helpful, I can schedule a 30-min walk-through with Carlos and your infra team to show the streaming demo. Proposed times: Monday 10am PT or Tuesday 2pm PT.

Cheers,
Rishi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwoodinference.com
